analysis: Both units are base-side excerpts (lines 28170-29783) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. They hold a Gemma long_prompt vector: repeated token IDs, a request_body/provider_body/template_input triple, and a plan with prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries and chain hashes. This region is not in the changed ranges; base changes sit at lines 3024-4824 and 43813-54138. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not view the head side of those changes. The visible patch shows a prompt-contract fixture update: it adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false to a Qwen-style vector, reduces prompt_token_count from 803 to 767, and changes the chain hashes and prompt_contract_id context. This is test-vector data only, with no code, authorization, attestation, key handling or transport logic. It touches no TB-002 or TB-011 control directly. The security-relevant cache context is T-041: chain hashes and prompt_contract_id feed prefix-cache keying, so these fixtures must agree with the runtime tokenizer/template. A mismatch between fixtures and the Swift provider's template or hash implementation would be a correctness problem, not something shown here to be exploitable. I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm the provider code that consumes these vectors (the prompt-contract hash and cache key derivation) was updated consistently. It should also confirm enable_thinking=false cannot cause cross-tenant cache key collisions, i.e. that the flag is included in prompt_contract_id or the chain. The head-side hunks of the changed ranges were not fully visible.
